title: 2D Pattern Information
content: **New in 2026.0** **** Access all the information needed for sampling and production in one place, and view and switch between different pattern revisions. 1. Go to 2D »**Pattern Information** in the top menu. → The Pattern Information window appears at the bottom of the CLO, Displaying a list of the current 2D patterns along with their information. 2. View and edit the information below as needed. **Information** | **Description** ---|--- **Item No.** | View or edit the pattern's number or code. **Image** | Preview the pattern shape as an image. **Name** | View or edit the pattern name. **Type** | View or set the pattern's type. • Shell • Lining • Facing • Binding • Neck Tape • Sleeve Head • Piping **Fabric** | View or change the fabric assigned to the pattern. **Grainline** | View or adjust the grainline angle of the pattern. **Shrinkage** | View and apply the pattern's horizontal and vertical shrinkage based on the fabric properties. **Mirror** | Select the axis used to mirror the pattern. Mirror determines whether the pattern is flipped horizontally or vertically when the Cut Amount is 2 or greater. _*_ For [symmetric patterns](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000354528-Linked-Editing#h_01J7NC8M60KYKRKZ07PXS4M1N1), the Horizontal axis is applied automatically and cannot be changed manually. To use a different axis, first remove the linked editing. **Cut Amount** | Set a cut amount of the pattern. * Cut Amount is automatically set based on whether [Linked Editing](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000354528-Linked-Editing#h_01J7NC8M60KYKRKZ07PXS4M1N1) is enabled for the pattern. **Description** | Add notes or comments related to the pattern. **Stage** | Set the current stage of the pattern. • Drafting: The pattern is in the initial development stage. • Editing: The pattern is being modified for design or fit adjustments. • Production: The pattern is finalized and ready for production. **Version History** | Track and restore the revision history for each pattern. Click ![Historty.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/59636802821529) **History** button on the right to save the current state of the pattern as a version. You can restore any previously saved version whenever needed.
content_description: Discover a centralized hub for managing and editing pattern information, including revisions, fabric details, and production stages, all designed to streamline your sampling and production processes in 2026.0.

title: If I have a fabric swatch, can it be simulated in CLO?
content: **Question** If I have a fabric swatch, can it be simulated in CLO? **Answer** To accurately simulate your fabric swatch in CLO, you need CLO's Fabric Kit or MDS which needs additional charges. However, Fabric Kit and MDS (Material Digitization Service) are ancillary services provided only to companies. The company must be qualified for CLO Business plan (One-person company is not eligible for using the MDS service and Fabric Kit). On the other hand, CLO does provide some emulated fabrics as default assets as well as [CLOFAB](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/49343947711769-CLOFAB) inside the CLO software and you can purchase other varieties of free emulated fabrics in [CLO-SET CONNECT](https://connect.clo-set.com/) which can be modified as needed. Please refer to the manual to learn how to edit [fabric properties](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/sections/115000716127-Fabric-Properties-) in CLO. Please [contact us](https://www.clo3d.com/contact) if you would like to purchase the Fabric Kit and use the FDS service,
content_description: Discover how to accurately simulate your fabric swatch in CLO and explore available resources, including the Fabric Kit and MDS services, while learning about default emulated fabrics and modification options.

title: Does CLO come with default Avatars?

You can find the default avatars in the avatar folder of the CLO library. On the software screen, the **Library button is located at the top right in blue** , and **the shortcut key is 'Y'** on the keyboard. **Here are the steps to get the default avatars:** 1. **Identifying the 'N' Mark** * On the Library screen, the 'N' mark located at the top right corner of the avatar thumbnail indicates that a download is required. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/48738868842137) 2. **Hovering Over the Avatar** * When you hover your mouse over the avatar thumbnail, a selection box appears in the top left corner of the thumbnail. 3. **Selecting the Avatar** 1. After selecting the avatar, a download link will appear on the right side of the Library popup. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/48738868843673) 4. **Downloading and Using the Avatar** * Once downloaded, you can load and use the avatar as needed. Moreover, you can also find more free avatars, hair, and poses via [CONNECT ](https://connect.clo-set.com/portfolio/208988/collection)

title: Corporate Firewall Setup and Allow-listing CLO Endpoints
content: ### Applicable for: Enterprise users who using corporate firewall and allow-listing policies First, make sure you have corporate firewalls and allow-listing policies in place on your network systems. If you are not familiar with this, please contact your company's IT and/or security team for this setup. Non-firewalled customers will not need to do this. Also, you do not need to configure the settings below for the firewall provided by Windows and macOS. ### Note * CLO authentication servers only allow HTTPS communication. Therefore, only port 443 is discussed in this article. * Until CLO 6.1, the **verify: peer** option inside the CLO software was **disabled**. But from CLO 6.2, the **verify: peer** option has been **enabled**. So if your company uses **SSL Inspection** on your secure network system, please check its detailed settings. Again, if your security system has SSL Inspection running, change that option. You will be able to make optional changes only for the CLO software. * If you are experiencing problems downloading in-app assets, add the domain ***.clo-set.com** to your allow-list. * A prominent security service that uses SSL Inspection is Zsclaer™, you can learn more about [**SSL Inspection on their webpage**](https://www.zscaler.com/resources/security-terms-glossary/what-is-ssl-inspection)**.** ## 1 Add below info in your corporate firewall settings * **CLO auth-server IPs** * 52.1.24.50 _(for all regions)_ * 52.20.29.14 _(this is only for mainland-China)_ * **Domains to be allowed** * *.clo3d.com * *.clo-set.com * **Protocol and port** * https / 443 port ## 2 Enable the Firewall option in CLO login window * Note that the information provided below is only for customers using corporate firewall solutions, not Windows or macOS firewall features. Check with your company's IT or security team whether you use a firewall. ![v2024_using_firewall.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/30795316023065)
content_description: This web page provides essential guidance for enterprise users on configuring corporate firewalls and allow-listing policies to ensure seamless access to CLO services while adhering to security protocols.

title: Create Notch
content: **List of Contents** Create Manually Create with Specific Values Add Point to Notch **Objective** Create notch on Pattern outlines as desired to improve sewing accuracy. **Location** Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Create ▶ **Notch** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![notch.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024295408/notch.png) **Notch** **Operation** **Create Manually** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. 2. Hover the mouse over the Pattern outline where the notch is to be added. → A notch is created and the [notch properties](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115013369268-Edit-Notch-Properties) appear in the Property Editor. **※Note:** Right-click on a point with Edit Pattern or Edit Curve Point tool (ver 6.1) and click Add Notch, a notch is created at the point **Create with Specific Values ** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. ** ** 2. Right-click on the Pattern outline where notches should be added to access the pop-up window. Then, type in the desired values referring to the table below. ****** ****** **Split Into Two Lines** | Line 1 / Line 2 | The line will be divided into two lines based on the reference point which was created when you hover the mouse over and right click the segment. The shorter side is indicated as Line 1, and the longer side is indicated as Line 2. Enter the desired value in either Line 1 or Line 2 to split the segment into two lines. ---|---|--- Ratio | The ratio of the line to be split is 100%. The line can be divided into two lines based on the ratio. Enter the desired ratio in either Line 1 or Line 2 to split the segment into two lines. This function is often used split a line into two identical segments or to add a point at its 33.3%. **Split by Length** **** | Segment Length | Enter the segment length which the whole line should be divided according to the interval. To reverse the direction that points are added, select **Reverse Direction**. Number of Segments | Enter the number of segments the selected line should be divided into. It is set as 2 by default. Direction | Reverse the direction that points are added. **Uniform Split** | Enter the number of segments the line should be divided into. The line is equally divided accordingly. 3. The notches are created based on the chosen options. **Add Point to Notch** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. 2. Right-click on the notch and click Add Point to Notch. → A straight point is added to the notch. **※Note:** If there is a seam allowance in the pattern in which the notch was created, the notch also appears in the seam allowance. In addition, if a notch is created in the corner of a pattern with seam allowance, the notch appears randomly only in one seam allowance of both seams. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on creating and managing notches on pattern outlines to enhance sewing accuracy within CLO 3D software.

title: Seamline Rip
content: ## **New in 2026.1** **Create Seamline Rip** **Edit Seamline Rip** **Set Seamline Rip Properties** **Produce Rip Result** **Restore the Ripped Area** **** The**Seamline Rip Tool** allows part or all of a sewing line to be designated as a rip area, and simulates the effect of the actual fabric opening and fraying. After creating an **Seamline Rip** on a sewing line of a 3D garment or 2D pattern, adjust the **Rip** and **Fray** properties to create effects such as seam rupture, damaged garments, and worn fabric details. #### **Create Seamline Rip** ##### **Partial Creation** A **Seamline Rip** can be created on a **Sewing Line**. 1. Select the **Seamline Rip Tool** from the **3D Toolbar**. 2. Move the mouse over the sewing line where the Rip object will be created on the 3D garment or 2D pattern. → A **Preview Point** appears at the position where creation is available. 3. Click on the sewing line to set the **Start Point**. → The **Start Point** is also displayed at the corresponding position on the **Paired Sewing Line**. 4. Move the mouse along the same sewing line. → A **Preview Line** is displayed from the **Start Point** to the current position. 5. Click another position on the sewing line to set the **End Point**. → A green **Rip object** is created between the **Start Point** and **End Point**. 6. The created **Seamline Rip** remains selected. → The **Seamline Rip** properties are displayed in the **Property Editor**. **Batch Creation** 1. Activate the **Sewing Tool** and select all Sewing Lines where Seamline Rips will be created. 2. Right-click to open the **Sewing Line Context Menu**. 3. Run **Add Seamline Rip**. 4. Select the **Edit Rip** tool and confirm that Seamline Rips have been created to fully cover the selected Sewing Lines **📝****Note:** * **Seamline Rip** can only be created on a **Sewing Line**. A single **Rip object** can only be created within one **Sewing Line** and cannot continue across another connected Sewing Line. * When a Rip object is created by the user, a **Paired****Seamline Rip** is also created and synchronized on the opposite Sewing Line corresponding to the source Sewing Line. * However, the properties that control ripping can be set individually. A Rip object cannot be created multiple times on the same Vertex of the same Sewing Line. #### **Edit Seamline Rip** Created Rip objects can be edited by adjusting their length, moving their position, deleting them, or editing their properties. 1. Select the **Edit Rip Tool**. 2. Select the Rip object to edit. → The **Start Point** , **End Point** , and **Line** of the selected Rip are highlighted. → The **Paired****Seamline Rip** is also displayed. 3. Drag the **Start Point** or **End Point** to adjust the length. 4. Drag the **Rip Line** to move its position along the same Sewing Line. 5. Release the mouse button to confirm the change. **📝****Note:** * When the length or position of a Rip is changed, subsequent simulation is performed based on the updated area. * If simulation is run after deleting a Rip, the previously ripped section is merged again. #### **Set Seamline Rip Properties** When an **Seamline Rip** is selected, **Rip** and **Fray** properties can be set in the **Property Editor**. ##### **Rip Properties** **Rip Properties** define the conditions for the specified **Seamline Rip** area to tear in real time in response to force applied during simulation. **Name** | **Description** ---|--- **Activate** | Enables the ripping effect of the Rip. When set to **On** , ripping occurs in real time once a certain force threshold is reached. **Restore on Deactivation** | When simulation is run after turning **Activate** Off, the previously ripped area is merged again while keeping the Rip object. **Rip Resistance** | **Rip Resistance** controls the seam’s resistance to tearing. It is calculated internally from Yield Strength, the force threshold at which damage begins, and Damage Rate, the rate at which damage accumulates over time. Lower values make the seam easier to tear; higher values increase its resistance to sustained force. ##### **Fray Properties** **Fray Properties** are used to represent fabric wear or fraying around the outline of the ripped **Seamline**. **Name** | **Description** ---|--- **Preset** | Saves the Fray properties as a **ZFRAY** file so they can be reused. The Preset list is synchronized with the corresponding folder. Path: C:\Users\Public\Documents\CLO\CLO Assets\Fabric\Fray ※ Note: The **Preset List** is synchronized with the **ZFRAY****files** in the folder. **Common** | **Activate** | Controls whether all Fray components are enabled. All other Fray elements are displayed only when this is turned on. It is recommended to keep this option enabled. **Generation** | **Fray Distance Threshold (mm)** | Defines the "Distress Region": when the two sides of the rip surface are below this threshold, it is considered a "Distress Region" rather than fully ripped. **Bridge Probability** | Probability that, within the "Distress Region" a fray will remain a bridge as a Loose Warp rather than be generated as a Fuzz. **Root Offset (mm)** | How far the root is offset into the edge it lives on. **Variation** | **Thickness Variation** | Randomness added to fray thickness. **Arch Variation** | Randomness added to "Arch" parameter in certain fray types. **Wavy Variation** | Randomness added to "Wavy" for certain fray types. **Gravity** | **Gravity Gravity** | Sets the strength of the gravity effect. **Gravity Direction X** | X-direction for gravity. **Gravity Direction Y** | Y-direction for gravity. **Gravity Direction Z** | Z-direction for gravity. **Material** | **Use Fabric Material** | Apply the Fabric's material properties to all Fray objects. **Fuzz** | **Activate** | Sets whether to draw **Fuzz** on the screen. This works only when **Activation** under **Common** is turned on. **Basic** | **Density (/mm)** | How many frays to generate per millimeter? **Thickness (mm)** | Base thickness of the fray. **Coverage (%)** | Randomly thins out the thread generation. **Length (mm)** | Length of the generated fray. **Length Variation** | Defines how much the length parameter varies by. **Taper** | Defines the ending radius of the fray. **Taper Variation** | Amount of randomness added to the taper field. **Segments** | Maximum number of segments used to model the fray. **Orientation** | **Lean Probability** | Defines the likelihood that a fray will have the "lean" effect added. Basically a deform leaning the fray to the left with a strength depending on the internal value. **Lean Strength** | Lean strength, if a fray gets the lean effect, it will be blended with a constant direction (towards the other side of the rip, generated once at generation time). **Rotation (°)** | Rotates the strand about its generation axis. **Grain Angle (°)** | This is supposed to rotate the frays at an angle within the plane of the seam. **Eyelash Rolling** | Intended to give an eyelash curling effect, curling the entire fray geometry. **Curl** | **Curliness** | Defines how many times the fray tries to spiral. **Curling Width** | Defines how wide the spiral curve of the fray will get. **Damping Power** | Damp out the curvature at the end of the fray. **Spiral Noise Strength** | Strength of noise added to the angular curling of the fray. **Spiral Noise Frequency** | Frequency of the noise applied to the angular curling of the fray. **Radial Noise Strength** | Strength of the noise added to the radial curling of the fray. **Radial Noise Frequency** | Frequency of the noise added to the radial curling of the fray. **Height Noise Strength** | Strength of noise added to the spacing of segment knots. **Height Noise Frequency** | Frequency of noise added to the spacing of segment knots. **Clumping** | **Clumping Radius** | Number of strands per clump, should be an integer value. **Clumping Damping Power** | Clumping strength. **Material** | **Color** | Sets the base color of the fray strands. **Glossiness** | Controls the strength and sharpness of surface reflections. **Softness** | Controls the perceived softness of the fray strands. **Loose** | **Warp** | **Activate** | Sets whether to draw **Loose Warp** on the screen. This works only when **Activation** under **Common** is turned on. **Basic** | **Density (mm)** | Number of loose warp threads to generate per edge. **Thickness (mm)** | Base thickness of the fray. **Segments** | Maximum number of segments used to model the fray. **Shape** | **Asymmetry** | Asymmetry of the wavy fray. **Arch** | Arch amplitude of thread. **Wavy Strength** | Amplitude of the waves, centered on fray. **Frequency** | Frequency of the fray waves. **Material** | **Color** | Sets the base color of the fray strands. **Glossiness** | Controls the strength and sharpness of surface reflections. **Softness** | Controls the perceived softness of the fray strands. **Weft** | **Activate** | Sets whether to draw **Loose Weft** on the screen. This works only when **Activation** under **Common** is turned on. **Basic** | **Density (mm)** | How many loose wefts to generate per edge pair. **Thickness (mm)** | Base thickness of the fray. **Segments** | Maximum number of segments used to model the fray. **Shape** | **Asymmetry** | Asymmetry of the wavy fray. **Arch** | Arch amplitude of fray from the seam edge. **Wavy Strength** | Amplitude of the waves, centered on fray. **Frequency** | Frequency of the fray waves. **Material** | **Color** | Sets the base color of the fray strands. **Glossiness** | Controls the strength and sharpness of surface reflections. **Softness** | Controls the perceived softness of the fray strands. **Exposed** | **Generation** | **Density (/mm)** | Density of exposed weft parameters. **Exposed Weft Snapping Probability** | Probability with which an exposed weft will stay an exposed weft rather than "snap" and become an exposed warp **Clumping** | **Clumping Radius (mm)** | World space distance along the seam that determines clumps (all strands within this distance will clump together). **Clumping Strength** | Strength of clumping effect **Weft** | **Activate** | Sets whether to draw **Exposed Warp** on the screen. This works only when **Activation** under **Common** is turned on. **Basic** | **Thickness (mm)** | Base thickness of the fray. **Segments** | Maximum number of segments used to model the fray. **Shape** | **Arch** | Arch controls the height of the arch formed by the exposed weft curves. **Asymmetry** | Asymmetry of the wavy fray. **Wavy Strength** | Amplitude of the waves, centered on fray. **Frequency** | Frequency of the fray waves. **Material** | **Color** | Sets the base color of the fray strands. **Glossiness** | Controls the strength and sharpness of surface reflections. **Softness** | Controls the perceived softness of the fray strands. **Warp** | **Activate** | Sets whether to draw **Exposed Weft** on the screen. This works only when **Activation** under **Common** is turned on. **Basic** | **Thickness (mm)** | Base thickness of the fray. **Segments** | Maximum number of segments used to model the fray. **Shape** | **Length (mm)** | Length of the generated fray **Length Variation** | Defines how much the length parameter varies by **Taper** | Defines the ending radius of the fray. **Taper Variation** | Amount of randomness added to the taper field. **Curl** | **Spiral Noise Strength** | Strength of noise added to the angular curling of the fray. **Spiral Noise Frequency** | Frequency of the noise applied to the angular curling of the fray. **Radial Noise Strength** | Strength of the noise added to the radial curling of the fray. **Radial Noise Frequency** | Frequency of the noise added to the radial curling of the fray. **Height Noise Strength** | Strength of noise added to the spacing of segment knots. **Height Noise Frequency** | Frequency of noise added to the spacing of segment knots. **Material** | **Color** | Sets the base color of the fray strands. **Glossiness** | Controls the strength and sharpness of surface reflections. **Softness** | Controls the perceived softness of the fray strands. **📝****Note:** * Fray is **Rendering****-only** and cannot be exported as geometry. * **macOS** is not supported yet. * Fray is displayed when two patterns connected by a Seamline are ripped. Therefore, it is recommended to adjust the Fray property values after the Seamline Rip has been torn and the Fray is visible. * If you need to use Fray repeatedly, it is recommended to save the desired Fray settings as a **Preset file (*.zfray)** and reuse them. * The Fray shape can be adjusted by changing the property values even when simulation is not running. #### **Produce Rip Result** During simulation, force above the threshold can be applied to tear the prepared **Seamline Rip** area. 1. Prepare a garment with a Rip applied. 2. Select the Seamline Rip object, then turn on the **Activate** in the **Property Editor**. 3. Run simulation. 4. Apply tension to the sewing line using an external force such as **Pinching**. 5. When the tension satisfies the **Rip Resistance** condition, the sewing line is ripped. 6. Check the ripped result and the **Fray** expression. 7. While simulation is running, adjust the **Fray** properties to refine the visual result. **📝****Note:** * If the length or position of the Rip is changed, or if the Rip is deleted during simulation, the running simulation stops. * **Rip** and **Fray** property values can be changed during simulation. * If the result is not as intended, use the **Edit Rip Tool** to adjust the length or position, then run simulation again. #### **Restore the Ripped Area** The ripped state can be restored to the original sewn state. 1. Select the **Seamline Rip**. 2. Check the **Restore on Deactivation** option. 3. Turn off **Activate**. 4. Run simulation. → The ripped sewing line is restored to its original state. **📝****Note:** * **Restore Rip** restores the ripped result while keeping the Rip object. * **Delete Rip** deletes the Rip object itself.
content_description: The Seamline Rip Tool enables users to create and edit realistic fabric rips and frays in 3D garments or 2D patterns, enhancing the visual detail of damaged or worn textiles.

title: Adjust Avatar Size
content: #### **List of Contents** ▪ Open Avatar Editor ▪ Adjust Size ▫ Overall Body Size ▫ Cup Size ▪ Adjust Shape ▪ Open/Save AVS File #### **Create an avatar with your own measurements.** **As CLO Avatar Editor is powered by thousands of real body scan data, even measurements not assigned by users automatically adjust to the most realistic body shape.** #### #### **Open Avatar Editor** 1. Open [CLO Avatar File (.avt).](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/ko/articles/115002687268) 2. Click the Main Menu » Avatar »**Avatar Editor** menu. #### #### **Adjust Size** ![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/38383105947289) #### ** Overall Body Size ** Sets the overall body size of the avatar. It is automatically adjusted based on actual body shape data according to the entered width and height measurements. 1. adjust the size if needed. **Option** | **Description**** ** ---|--- **Size**** **** **** **| **Width**** **| **Bust** | Set the overall body width based on the bust circumference. **Under Bust** | Set the overall body width based on the under bust circumference. Set the type of Width to Under Bust, then adjusting the detailed measurements of Bust allows you to change the cup size while maintaining the overall body shape. **Weight** | Set the overall body width by entering the weight. **Height** | **Total Height** | Enter the height measured from the ground to the head. **📝****Note:** Since each person has a different head size, it is most accurate to create a overall body shape based on HPS Height or Inseam, rather than Total Height, which is less accurate and not recommended. **HPS Height** | Enter the height measured from the ground to the neck. **Inseam** | Enter the height measured from the ground to the crotch. **Detailed Mesurements** | Click the link button to unlink and modify the width and height while keeping detailed measurements. title: Internal Line Variable Fold Angle
content: **New in 2026.1** **** Apply a fold angle that tapers from one end of an internal line to the other, creating smoother and more gradual folds across a pattern (e.g., a front crease on formal trousers). **** 1. title: HASP Error Message
content: **List of Contents** Communication error between local and remote Sentinel HASP License Managers (H0040) Feature not found (H0031) Sentinel HASP key not found (H0007) Too many concurrent useres (H0038) Unable to access Sentinel HASP Run-time Environment(H0033) **Communication error between local and remote Sentinel HASP License Managers (H0040)** **Cause of Error** The Server and Client PCs are unable to communicate with each other. **Solution** 1. Type 'services.msc' in the Run window. ![1.jpg](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360077798874/1.jpg) 2. In the Service window that follows, check whether or not the status of the ‘Sentinel LDK License Manager’ is ‘Running’. If the status is not ‘Running’, right click and select **Start**. If the status is ‘Started’, right click and select **Restart**. Reboot. ![33.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360000410167/33.png) 3. If this does not solve the problem, check both versions of the Server and Client PC’s HASP Drivers. Make sure both versions are the same. You are able to check the version under Diagnostics. ![image.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360077799894/image.png) 4. If this does not work, ask your Network Administrator to confirm the Port communication status between the Server and Client. Check whether the 1947 Port is being used by another program. **Feature not found (H0031)** **Cause of Error** Despite the dongle key has been recognized, the Feature ID of the program and the Feature ID of the dongle key are different. (This occurs when the wrong version of CLO 3D is installed - i.e. installed the Stand-Alone version for a Network dongle key, and vice versa) **Solution** Make sure the correct version of CLO 3D is installed. ex> Purchased the Network version, but used the Stand-Alone version's installer. -> Re-install CLO 3D using the Network version's installer. **Sentinel HASP key not found (H0007)** **Objective** **Cause of Error** \- When the HASP Key is not plugged in to the PC. \- Network Version only: the Client PC does not recognize the Server PC that the dongle key is connected to. \- When the HASP Key is recognized, but the Sentinel License Manager service fails to start properly. **Solution** Make sure the HASP is connected to the PC. 1. Check the red light of the HASP Key. It should light up when plugged in to the PC. 2. Check whether or not the HASP Key shows up in the [ACC page](http://localhost:1947/) (refer to the image below). ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115000784388/Sentinel_HASP_key_not_found__H0007_.png) 3. If the red light, or the ACC page does not look equal to the image above, refer to the following manual, reinstall the Sentinel HASP Driver. [Sentinel HASP Driver Manual Installation](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000558507-%EC%84%A4%EC%B9%98-%ED%9B%84-%EB%B0%9C%EC%83%9D%ED%95%A0-%EC%88%98-%EC%9E%88%EB%8A%94-%EB%AC%B8%EC%A0%9C-%ED%95%B4%EA%B2%B0-%EB%B0%8F-%EB%B0%A9%EB%B2%95) **Too many concurrent users (H0038)** **Cause of Error** When the number of users connected to the program exceeds the maximum allowed number of users. ex> If the maximum number of users (the number of purchased licenses) is 2, and 3 users try to log-in, the last person to attempt a connection will receive an error message. **Solution** Check the number of current users via the link below. Connect when one of the current users exit the program. [ACC Page ](http://localhost:1947/) Click **Sentinel Keys** , on the left. When the Key shows up as the image above, click **Sessions** , on the right. The following page should display the current user(s). Connect when one of the current users exits the program. If any unauthorized user is connected, click the **Disconnect** button on the right to log the person out of the program. **Unable to access Sentinel HASP Run-time Environment(H0033)** **Cause of Error** The HASP Driver has not been properly installed on the PC, or the Driver is damaged. To confirm whether it being properly installed, enter [http://localhost:1947](http://localhost:1947/) or [http://127.0.0.1:1947](http://127.0.0.1:1947%EC%9D%84/) into your web browser, or click on the following link ( [ACC Page](http://127.0.0.1:1947/) ). If the following page does not look equal to the image below, there is a problem with the Sentinel HASP Driver. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115000736287/Unable_to_access_Sentinel_HASP_Run-time_Environment_H0033_.png) **Solution** Refer to the following manual and reinstall the HASP Driver. [HASP Driver Installation ](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000558507-%EC%84%A4%EC%B9%98-%ED%9B%84-%EB%B0%9C%EC%83%9D%ED%95%A0-%EC%88%98-%EC%9E%88%EB%8A%94-%EB%AC%B8%EC%A0%9C-%ED%95%B4%EA%B2%B0-%EB%B0%8F-%EB%B0%A9%EB%B2%95) Go Back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides troubleshooting solutions for common Sentinel HASP License Manager errors, including communication issues, license recognition failures, and installation problems.

title: How do I start a CLO free trial version?
content: # **Quick Overview** CLO offers a 14-day CLO free trial for users eligible for an Individual license. Your paid CLO subscription will automatically start right after the trial expires, but you can cancel before renewal to avoid charges. Students must verify their status prior to starting the trial to receive a student discount. --- ## **Important Note for Students** To receive the student discount, you must verify your student status before starting your CLO free trial. If you fail to do so, you will not be eligible for the discount. For more details, please see: [Does CLO offer student discounts?](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115013366988-Does-CLO-offer-student-discounts) ## **Eligibility for a CLO Free Trial** A CLO Trial License can be started via the subscription button on the CLO web and is strictly reserved for a hobbyist, freelancer, self-employed individual, or one-person company who qualifies for a CLO Individual License according to our [Terms of Service](https://legal.clo-set.com/additional-clo) (2.2.1). *Enterprise and Academic entities must contact the CLO Business Development Team via Contact Us separately to obtain the appropriate CLO Trial License. ## **Start Your CLO Free Trial** You must sign up first if you don't have a CLO account yet. 1. Click the **FREE TRIAL** button on the main banner or at the top right side of [clo3d.com](https://www.clo3d.com/en/) or the 'GET STARTED' button on the [CLO subscription page](https://clo3d.com/en/plans). 2. Choose the CLO license plan. * The chosen CLO plan will get started automatically after your trial expiration. 3. Review your order, enter your billing address, and click the 'Continue' button. 4. Enter your payment information on the final checkout page. * If you have already used the same payment information with other CLO accounts, you will see a payment failure. Then, please click the 'SKIP Trial' button. 5. Download a CLO installer and start your CLO free trial. *If you have already downloaded the CLO trial version, you can go to the [CLO download page](https://clo3d.com/en/clo/download) for a CLO installer. ## **Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)** ### **What happens after the CLO free trial expires?** Your paid CLO subscription will automatically start right after the 14-day trial expires. You can cancel your trial before renewal to avoid any charges. ### **How can Enterprise and Academic entities obtain a CLO Trial License?** Enterprise and Academic entities must contact the CLO Business Development Team via Contact Us separately to obtain the appropriate CLO Trial License, as the standard web trial is for Individual Licenses only. ### **Do I need to verify my student status to get a CLO discount after the trial?** Yes, to receive the student discount, you must verify your student status before starting your CLO free trial. If you fail to do so, you will not be eligible for the discount.
content_description: Discover how to start your 14-day free trial of CLO, ensuring you qualify for an Individual license and explore student discounts with proper verification.

title: Viewport Camera
content: ## **New in 2026.1** **Import Cameras** **Export Cameras** **Set Main Camera** **Delete Camera** **Default Camera** **** Camera data can be imported and exported with supported 3D file formats to preserve scene views across different software environments. #### **Import Camera** Camera objects can be imported from supported **FBX** and **glTF 2.0 (glTF/GLB)** files. 1. Go to **File > Import > ****FBX** or **glTF 2.0 (glTF** or **GLB)**. 2. In the **Import** dialog, enable **Cameras** in the **Object** section. → Camera objects included in the file are imported with the scene. 3. Click **OK** to import the file. → Imported cameras are added to the scene and displayed in the Scene Graph. #### **Export Camera** Camera objects can be exported with supported **FBX** and **glTF 2.0 (glTF/GLB)** files. 1. Go to **File > Export > FBX **or **glTF 2.0 (glTF/GLB)** 2. In the **Export FBX** dialog, enable **Include****Camera** in the **Object** section. → Camera objects in the scene are included in the exported FBX file. 3. Click **OK** to export the file. #### **Set Main Camera** A camera in the Scene Graph can be set as the **Main Camera** from the context menu. The Main Camera is used as the active camera for scene viewing and workflows that require a representative camera view. 1. In the **Scene Graph** , right-click the camera you want to use as the Main Camera. 2. Select **Set as Main Camera** from the context menu. → The selected camera is set as the Main Camera. 3. The Main Camera status is updated in the Scene Graph. → The selected camera is displayed as the current Main Camera. #### **Delete Camera** Camera objects can be deleted from the Scene Graph. 1. In the **Scene Graph** , right-click the camera you want to delete. 2. Select **Delete** from the context menu. → The selected camera is deleted immediately. → The camera is removed from the Scene Graph. **※ Note:** The **Default Camera** cannot be deleted. The **Delete** action is disabled for the Default Camera. #### **Default Camera** A scene always requires a Default Camera. If a scene does not contain a camera with the Default flag, a new **Default Camera** is created when **New Project** is executed.
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide to the new camera management features in version 2026.1, including import/export options, setting the main camera, and managing default and custom camera objects in 3D scenes.

title: Blend Shape Avatar
content: **New in 2026.0** **** Blend Shape is a technology that creates natural forms by blending various pre-made body types or facial expressions at desired ratios. With just a single base model, Blend Shape allows for real-time and flexible transformations, ranging from various target body sizes to subtle facial expressions. This feature enables users to import avatars containing Blend Shape data into CLO, allowing for instantaneous body changes and precise dynamic fitting. **📝****Note:** To use this feature, you should import files that contain Blend Shape data. #### **Blend Shape** 1. Load a file containing Blend Shape data as an Avatar type. 2. Go to Main Menu → Avatar → **Avatar Editor** to open the Avatar Editor 3. Click on the **Blend Shape** tab in the Avatar Editor 4. Check the list of **Deformable Parameters** included in the loaded avatar. 5. Adjust the weight of the desired part between 0 and 100 to modify the shape. #### #### **Set Options** 1. **Select Avatar** * This option is displayed when multiple Blend Shape avatars are loaded; it will not appear if only a single avatar is present. * Selecting an avatar will display the corresponding Deformable Parameters for that specific avatar. 2. **Deformable Parameters** * The list of deformable parameters included by the creator is grouped and displayed by mesh unit. * Each parameter can be set as a **Favorite**. By enabling **Show Favorites Only** in the top right, you can manage the list efficiently by displaying only your favorited items. * Clicking the **Reset** button will revert all unsaved changes to their initial values. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/60054467384473) Enable **Show Selected Only** to display only the items related to the selected **3D Avatar** part. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/60054467384473) #### **Blend Shape Animation** * Click **Add Animation Keyframe** on the right side of a **Deformable Parameter** list item to set the corresponding property value as a keyframe at the **Current Frame**. * **Blend Shape Animation** can be imported and exported using **FBX, glTF/GLB, Alembic, and USD** file formats.

title: 3D Pencil (Avatar)
content: **New in 2026.0** Sketch Set Options Convert to 3D Pen **** Sketch directly on the avatar and turn your lines into patterns instantly. #### **Sketch** 1. [Open an avatar](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115002687268-Avatar-AVT-Open-Add-Save#h_01KJBWPJ36BCHSD19S856T5RK5) in the 3D window to being sketching. 2. In the 3D toolbar, press and hold the **![3D Pen Avatar On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55500528789785)3D Pen (Avatar)** and switch to the ![3D Pencil Avatar On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55500553607449) **3D Pencil (Avatar)**. → The Sketch window appears, and the viewpoint switches to the front view. **📝****Note:** To ensure proper conversion to 3D Pen after sketching, the 3D view is fixed to either the front or back view. Only zooming is available. 3. Click and drag on the avatar to sketch your design. 4. Change the type to **![Eraser.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55500528790937)Eraser** , then click and drag over the area you want to remove. → The lines within the dragged area are removed. #### **Set Options** 1. Set the following options as needed. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Type** | **Pencil** | **Symmetry** | Applies symmetrical sketching based on the avatar’s center axis. **Conversion** **Guide** | Before converting to 3D Pen, you can see how your sketch will be converted. The segment points shown on the guide line are important, as areas without points will turn into curves. If you need a corner or a defined angle, make sure a point is present at that position. If a corner is missing a point, the edge may become rounded unintentionally. We recommend reviewing the guide and adjusting your lines to achieve the best results before converting. **Eraser** | **Size** | Adjust the eraser size to control how much is removed at once. **Viewpoint** | Switch the 3D viewpoint to either the front or back. #### **Convert to 3D Pen** 1. Click the **Convert to 3D Pen** in the Sketch window. → The lines drawn on the avatar are converted to 3D Pen, and the tool automatically switches to the ![Edit 3D Pen Avatar On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55500528791961)**Edit 3D Pen (Avatar).** 2. Check the converted 3D Pen and [edit ](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115008890367-Edit-3D-Pen-Avatar)it directly as needed. _**✨Tip:** For 3D Pens created by sketching on both the front and back simultaneously,_[_flattening_](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115008890627-Flatten) _both sides automatically sews the front and back together._

title: I cannot log in. What should I do?
content: **Question** I cannot log in. What should I do? I cannot sign in on the CLO web or CLO software, even if I enter a valid ID and Password. I was charged for my subscription, but it says I don't have a license **Answer** Please follow the instructions below based on your subscription plan and software authentication for Business Plan Clients to solve the login issue. **CLO for Individuals** 1. Please use the Chrome browser over other browsers and remove the old cookies. 2. Check your user ID and Password (User ID and PW you set up when signing up clo3d website.) -For signing in to CLO software, the user ID is your email address above CLO 2024 version, or the name on your account page or receipt below 2024 version. -If you receive the user ID as your email address, please install CLO software with 2024 version via the [download page](https://clo3d.com/en/clo/download) and access CLO software through 'sign-in with CLO-SET'. -Please check your user ID from your subscription invoice as some users are confused with other CLO accounts. 3. Please check if you access the CLO software for an Individual license (Standalone Onlineauth). 1. If the CLO software is not Standalone Onlineauth, please go to the download page after signing in and install the right version. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/52747524784537) 4. If the PC's 443 port firewall is blocked, unblock and try logging in again. 5. Deactivate the antivirus program on the PC and try logging in again. 6. If the above steps do not solve your problem, please reach out via [Contact Us](http://clo3d.com/contact). **CLO for Business Users** **Standalone** 1. Check the dongle key is connected to the PC, and try logging in again. 2. Check the [HASP Driver](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000615488#Click3) is properly installed, and try logging in again. 3. Confirm internet connection. 4. Confirm ID and Password. 5. If the PC's 443 port firewall is blocked, unblock and try logging in again. 6. Deactivate the antivirus program on the PC and try logging in again. 7. If the above steps do not solve your problem, please reach out via [Contact Us](http://clo3d.com/contact). **Network** 1. Check the dongle key is connected to a PC in the same network service, and try logging in again. 2. Check the [HASP Driver](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000615488#Click3) is properly installed on the PC, and try logging in again. 3. Check your computer is in the same network service as the PC with the dongle key. 4. If your computer is not in the same network service, select port forwarding and try logging in again. **OnlineAuth** 1. Confirm ID and Password. 2. If the PC's 443 port firewall is blocked, unblock and try logging in again. 3. Deactivate the antivirus program on the PC and try logging in again. 4. If the above steps do not solve your problem, please reach out via [Contact Us](http://clo3d.com/contact).
content_description: This web page provides step-by-step troubleshooting instructions for users experiencing login issues with CLO software, tailored to both individual and business subscribers.
